chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the people take their places in Mina, a Caller calls out: 'Had you known of the court of the One you are being Welcomed by, you would have been convinced with the replacement (of your expenses) after the Forgiveness'.

key_terms.حَلَلْتُمْ: You have been welcomed or received (by the Host/God)
key_terms.فِنَاءُ: Court or precinct, referring to the presence of the Divine
key_terms.مُنَادٍ: A Caller, often interpreted as a divine or angelic announcer
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What does the Caller announce to pilgrims in Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reveals a hidden spiritual reality during the Hajj in Mina, where a divine Caller announces that the magnitude of the Divine Welcome guarantees not only forgiveness but also specific financial compensation (khalaf) for the pilgrims' expenditures. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the tangible and spiritual rewards of Hajj, linking the act of worship directly to divine economic justice and the certainty of recompense for those who truly comprehend the majesty of the encounter.
